newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakakibara says PM asked MOF to deal with forex.
newsitem.headline: Sakakibara says PM asked MOF to deal with forex.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has asked the Finance Ministry to deal appropriately with excessive foreign exchange movements, Eisuke Sakakibara, head of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said on Thursday.
"The prime minister has instructed us to act against forex moves in a timely and appropriate manner. We will act decisively against excessive forex moves," he told reporters.
Sakakibara said he did not think Japan's current account surplus was a major problem. "A drastic expansion of the surplus cannot happen," he said.

Asked what he thought about market participants focusing on Japan's surplus, he said: "I think the issue is being played up excessively. People should try to understand more clearly the position of the United States."
He added that U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers was due to make a speech tonight and is likely to comment on the issue.
